followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability scores and stated preferences.

On capability, Petrel is the stronger model across nearly every relevant metric — its summarization (84.5 vs 80.3) and creative generation (87.2 vs 78.8) eval scores both clear the variance threshold, and a synopsis request sits squarely in that recall-and-condense territory. So even on pure quality grounds, Petrel was the better pick.

The preference data reinforced rather than drove the decision. Your message was notably warm ("You're always great," "Thanks so much"), and Petrel self-reports rising win rates as tone moves from neutral to friendly. It also reports a strong positive slope for generative/open-format tasks, and a synopsis has some of that latitude. Lapwing, by contrast, only reports a distinctive (flat) preference profile around harm-adjacent content, which isn't relevant here — nothing about your request touches that dimension.

So Petrel won on capability and was at worst neutral, plausibly favorable, on preference fit. There was no consideration pulling toward Lapwing for this query.
